title: auth-api-401-429-debug-scratchpad-lena-2026-03-27
content:
Quick summary:
- Intermittent 401 and 429 errors observed from hosted API for a handful of customers across regions (primarily us-west1, eu-west1).
- Pattern: 401 spikes often immediately followed by bursts of 429s for same API keys. Looks like auth failure -> retries -> hitting quota/rate limits.
- Repro: can reproduce locally with a scripted load of 50 req/s using curl + wrong header rotation under api-key-abuse test key.

Timeline / breadcrumbs:
- 2026-03-25 09:12 PST: Pager alert (ops): elevated 5xx/4xx error rate for hosted endpoints.
- 2026-03-25 09:15 PST: First customer ticket (acct: acme-123) reports auth failures.
- 2026-03-25 09:20 PST: Observed 401 spikes in metrics for api_key=key-XXXX and immediate retry bursts in ingress (source: lb logs).
- 2026-03-25 09:25 PST: Automated client retries (backoff poorly configured) caused aggregated 429s; downstream quota throttling triggered.

Commands / requests I ran (local repro):
- curl (simple):
  curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-INVALID" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/complete
  -> returns 401 {"error":{"message":"Invalid API key","code":"unauthorized"}}

- scripted load (bash loop) to simulate retry storms:
  for i in $(seq 1 200); do \n    curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-INVALID" \n      -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-base-1\",\"input\":\"test\"}' \n      https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/complete &\n  done; wait

- Verified with valid key but rotated header:
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-VALID" -H "X-Client-Id: client-A" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/complete
  -> 200 for single call

- Bulk valid-key with high concurrency -> observe 429s:
  hey -n 1000 -c 100 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-VALID" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/complete
  -> many 429 responses, rate_limit headers present (X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0)

Error snippets (copied from logs):
- 401 responses:
  {"error":{"message":"Invalid API key","type":"invalid_request_error","code":"unauthorized"}}

- 429 responses:
  {"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded","type":"rate_limit_error","retry_after":2}}

Relevant logs from ingress (truncated):
- 2026-03-25T09:21:03Z lb-01 request_id=abc123 src=12.34.56.78 api_key=key-XXXX method=POST path=/v1/complete status=401 rt=23ms
- 2026-03-25T09:21:05Z lb-01 request_id=abc124 src=12.34.56.78 api_key=key-XXXX method=POST path=/v1/complete status=401 rt=18ms
- 2026-03-25T09:21:06Z lb-01 request_id=abc125 src=12.34.56.78 api_key=key-XXXX method=POST path=/v1/complete status=429 rt=12ms

Correlated backend traces (from jaeger):
- Trace shows initial auth check failed at auth-service (subsystem: token-verify). auth-service returned 401 with error "signature mismatch".
- Shortly after, client retried without exponential backoff; gateway rate-limited the client at quota-manager.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Client using an expired/rotated key -> auth-service returns 401 -> clients retry quickly -> aggregated retries trip per-key quota/rate limits -> see 429. (most likely)
2) Intermittent auth-service bug that sometimes rejects valid tokens due to cache sync issues (redis TTL mismatch) causing transient 401s. (medium)
3) Misrouting: requests hit an older auth-service deployment with stale public keys for signature verification -> 401s for subset of traffic. (possible; check deploy rollouts)
4) Quota accounting edge case: quota manager counts failed auth attempts toward rate limit/quota incorrectly. (low but important if true)

Evidence for / against hypotheses:
- For (1): Customer showed client SDK logs with wrong key rotation timing. We reproduced by using an invalid key and saw identical pattern.
- Against (2): auth-service logs don't show increased errors except for the failed token signature events tied to specific keys; no OOM/exception traces. Cache hit/miss rates look normal.
- For (3): Deployment history shows a canary of auth-service was rolled 2026-03-24 04:00 UTC; need to check if any instances still serving old certs/keys.
- For (4): Quota-manager code review TODO: confirm whether 401 responses should increment retry counters. Current instrumenting shows counters increment on request accept at gateway, before auth outcome. That might explain counting failed auth attempts.

Immediate next steps (what I did / to do):
- Checked deploys: kubectl get pods -n auth | grep auth-service -> all pods at v1.12.3 (rolled 3/24), no old revisions running (done).
- Instrumented gateway to log auth outcome + quota decision correlation (added temporary flag). Pushed and redeployed to canary gateway (canary: gw-canary-3).
- Action: Add temporary exception so failed auth (401) does NOT decrement/add to per-key quota counters while we investigate. Note: risky (permit abuse) so applied only to canary and enabled sampling.
- Reached out to solutions-eng to confirm customer key rotation schedules (Jordan).
- Repro script committed under my home dir: /home/lena/debug/auth-401-429-repro.sh (TODO: move to repo, link ticket).

Longer term / follow-ups:
- Update quota manager to only count successful auth requests toward burst/short-term throttles (design review with infra).
- Add monitoring alerts for correlated 401->429 patterns (if 401 spike leads to 429 within 5 min for same key).
- Add client guidance in SDKs to backoff exponentially and jitter on 401s (and avoid immediate retry with same key).
- Run a forensic sweep for any other services rolled around 3/24; double-check public key rotation and cert TTLs.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Could we add a short-lived grace-window after a 401 for the same key where quota manager ignores the next N retries? That would mitigate client mis-rotation storms.
- Check if rate limit headers are consistently returned on 401 responses; currently some 401s don't include rate-limit headers and that confuses clients.

Open questions / asks:
- Jordan: can you confirm acme-123 rotation schedule and whether they use SDK auto-rotate?
- Samir: can you audit quota-manager code path where we increment retry counters? I think increment happens pre-auth.
- SRE: should we keep the canary gateway exception for 24h and monitor? (I will revert after confirm)

Files & references:
- Repro script: /home/lena/debug/auth-401-429-repro.sh
- JIRA: JIRA-7892 (investigation ticket)
- Confluence runbook: confluence://ops/auth-rate-limit-runbook

Next-modify plan (today):
- 10:30 PST: run controlled repro against canary gateway for 15 minutes and observe quota counters.
- 11:30 PST: join call with Jordan & Samir to review logs and agree on next steps.

-- end of scratchpad --
